title: Gifts and fruits (CCC 1830–1832)
hookLine: seven gifts of the Spirit, twelve fruits

lines: A SHOOT FROM THE ROOT OF JESSE.
cards: "There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root." That's Isaiah, in the Douay-Rheims. An old root in the ground, and out of it, something green and new.
On that shoot, Isaiah says, the spirit of the Lord will rest, and he names what that spirit brings. Christians have read the passage as being about Jesus, the son of David, born of Jesse's line.
The Catechism takes Isaiah's list and says it doesn't stop with him.

teach.h: THE GIFTS: READY FOR THE SPIRIT.
teach.b: Back on day one hundred twenty-seven, at confirmation, you met the seven gifts, and on day five hundred eighty-one, the fruits. Today, how they fit. Virtues built by effort, the Catechism says, aren't the whole picture.
The moral life is also held up by the gifts of the Holy Spirit: lasting dispositions that make a person docile, ready to follow the Spirit's promptings.

Seven: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, and fear of the Lord. They belong in their fullness to Christ, son of David, and they finish and perfect the virtues of those who receive them.
Fortitude is courage that holds. Counsel is knowing what to do in a tangle. Fear of the Lord, as some teachers explain it, isn't terror but awe, the kind that keeps God God.
That's the root. Then the fruit.
The fruits of the Spirit, the Catechism says, are perfections the Spirit forms in a person, as the first fruits of eternal glory, and the Church's tradition lists twelve, from Galatians.
In the Douay-Rheims: "But the fruit of the Spirit is, charity, joy, peace, patience, benignity, goodness, longanimity, mildness, faith, modesty, continency, chastity." Benignity is kindness.
Longanimity is long, patient endurance, a slow fuse. Continency is self-control.

teach.h: THE ROOT IS HIDDEN, THE FRUIT FEEDS.
teach.b: A gift is received and hidden, like a root. A fruit shows on the branch, where others can see it and be fed. Nobody tastes your fortitude.
They taste your patience on a hard afternoon. The gifts are given; the fruits are how anyone can tell.

how: Catholics associate the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit with baptism and confirmation, where the bishop prays for them, and some learn the gifts and the twelve fruits by heart before confirmation.

games.q: a friend says, "I can't tell whether the Spirit is at work in me." by today's teaching, where would you look?

games.why: the gifts are hidden like a root. the fruits are what shows, and what feeds others.

practice: Go back over the last day or two, slowly, and look for one moment, in you or in someone near you, where one of those fruits showed up: patience in a checkout line, gentleness with a tired child, joy from nowhere, peace in a tense meeting.
Stay with it, and ask who was fed by it. If you pray, give thanks for it; if you don't, let it be noticed.

wordCard.voice: Gifts and fruits. The gifts of the Spirit, wisdom through fear of the Lord, make a person ready to follow God; the fruits, charity through chastity, are what grows and shows. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: gifts become fruit. The root hides; the fruit feeds. Until tomorrow.
